correctness.rationale: The input variation is unweighted distributional variation on the open interval. The beta moments orthogonalize 1,t,t²−1/(2p+1), and integrating the two nonconstant kernel terms over a step gives derivative A_p(a)(1+cat), with the stated positive prefactor. Its integrated absolute value equals A_p(a) times 2 or c|a|+1/(c|a|), depending on whether the affine zero is in the interval. The derivative on the second branch has sign opposite to Q_c(a²); for c>3 its exact signs at c^−2,c^−1,1 are +,−,+, so the larger root gives the unique positive off-centre local maximum. Comparison at a=c^(−1/2), using the displayed strict logarithmic bounds, makes this maximum strictly exceed the center for every p>0. Stieltjes superposition gives the exact BV norm and equality forces support on the two maximizing points. The two affine profiles agree in sign near zero but disagree on an endpoint interval, so no choice of two nonzero signed masses makes their signs agree almost everywhere. Only single jumps extremize. The beta normalization and root behavior (1−u_+ is of order p near zero; u_+∼1/c at infinity) give all stated limits. For p=1 the larger root is (12+√69)/75 and yields the stated decimals. Independent bounded scans of the step profile at seven shapes agreed with the radical optimum to 1e−9 in gain; this does not replace global proof.
residual_risks: Numerical grids do not establish off-centre optimality between sample points or parameter values. Those assertions follow from the analytical comparison.
